title: No Kings movement holds early voting rallies across US states
seoTitle: Los Angeles No Kings early voting rallies

tea.why: Organisers staged nationwide rallies to encourage voter participation and early voting ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
tea.want: To inspire eligible voters to make a plan, cast early ballots, and understand their voting options.
tea.changed: Oct 17: The No Kings movement held thousands of early voting rallies and events across all 50 states, including Los Angeles.

summary: The grassroots No Kings coalition, along with partner organisations like the American Civil Liberties Union, organised thousands of early voting rallies across the United States. Dubbed 'No Kings: Vote Early', the nationwide events on October 17 shifted focus from symbolic resistance against the administration to nonpartisan voter participation and get-out-the-vote efforts ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Activities varied widely by location, featuring events such as a music festival in Los Angeles, family workshops in Chicago, and election observer training in Atlanta. Organisers stated the initiative aimed to ensure eligible voters understand their voting options and have the opportunity to make their voices heard.
demands: Encourage citizens to cast early ballots in the midterm elections
Help eligible voters make a plan to vote
Ensure every eligible voter understands their voting options
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The No Kings movement held over 3,000 events across 50 states focusing on early voter turnout for the November midterms.
